A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Tora. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original video-generation comparisons, architectural and training ablations, qualitative results, and motion-VAE evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds DiT-based comparisons, model/data-scaling experiments, and a human preference study.

M1.justification: v4 adds CogVideoX-2B/5B adaptations that retain the backbone VAE for motion compression and insert MGF before the Expert Transformer's full-attention module (Section 4.3). v3 describes only OpenSora-based Tora; its core TE/MGF design and two-stage training remain.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 adds Pexels as a fourth reported training-video source, while retaining the video-generation task and 185-clip evaluation benchmark. However, Appendix 9.1 retains the earlier source list and 631,053-clip total, leaving the exact training-mixture change unresolved.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds OpenSora and OpenSora-based DragNUWA alongside the five retained UNet comparators; OpenSora previously appeared in qualitative comparisons. The new user study evaluates OpenSora-v1.2, CogVideoX-2B, Vidu, and Kling v1.0, substantially broadening the comparison set.

E3.justification: v4 introduces model/data-scaling experiments and a 10-volunteer pairwise evaluation of physics simulation, sensory quality, and instruction following, with volunteers drawing Tora's trajectories. Appendix preprocessing also changes the flow-score cutoff from greater than 2 to greater than 3. This reported revision does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Figure 7 add a substantive analysis testing motion-control accuracy against model size and training-data volume using two CogVideoX adaptations. The earlier compression, fusion, training-strategy, duration/resolution, and motion-VAE analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Dataset mean/standard-deviation reporting is unchanged; the added user study presents win rates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Previously reported benchmark, ablation, and motion-VAE numerical rows remain unchanged. v4 adds DiT-baseline results, scaling results, and human preferences: OpenSora-based DragNUWA reports 128-frame TrajError 21.75, while Tora's wins against Kling are 45%, 43%, and 41% for physics, sensory quality, and instruction following. Figures 1–2 also replace qualitative outputs.

T1.justification: Equation 6 replaces Conv with MLP in the extra-channel fusion mapping, matching the MLP already depicted in Figure 4. This corrects the mathematical description; the remaining equations and assumptions are unchanged, with no new theoretical derivation or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first trajectory-oriented DiT, novel TE/MGF modules, scalable conditional generation up to 204 frames at 720p, and improved motion realism. v4 makes comparative accuracy and the foundational-model comparison more explicit, but v3 already asserts these advantages and discusses OpenSora in its appendix.

C2.justification: v4 attributes the adapted DragNUWA baseline's visual degradation to incompatibility with DiT's latent space and interprets the scaling results as supporting module scalability. Its user-study discussion adds a comparative limitation: competitive results with Vidu but a remaining gap to Kling.

D1.justification: v4 supplies an explicit code repository link, adaptation details, and the L1 specification for TrajError; reported hardware changes from four to eight A100s. Conversely, it omits v3's 512×512 comparison resolution and 480p, 16:9, 204-frame ablation settings. These documentation changes do not themselves establish changed runs.

R1.justification: Related Work adds discussion of CogVideoX and DragAnything and citations including Movie Gen, Motion Prompting, ReVideo, Motion-I2V, and PUCA. The overall trajectory-control positioning remains; TrailBlazer is still cited and evaluated despite replacement of its descriptive sentence.

P1.justification: v4 numbers sections, updates affiliation text, edits sentences, and revises contribution/results paragraphs. Part of the earlier appendix comparison discussion is condensed into Figure 6's caption. Most method and appendix prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 replace example panels, Table 1 gains UNet/DiT groupings, and new Figure 7 and Table 5 display scaling and user-study results. Typesetting, captions, and float placement change, while architecture diagrams and most existing experimental displays retain their designs.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3's UNet-based main comparisons, v4's OpenSora-based DragNUWA control better tests the value of Tora's motion modules. Scaling and human studies add support and expose the gap to Kling. These gains are tempered by omitted evaluation settings, inconsistent training-source descriptions, and missing uncertainty estimates for human preferences.
